newsitem.title: USA: Va. Power North Anna 1 nuke restart unknown.
newsitem.headline: Va. Power North Anna 1 nuke restart unknown.

text.p: Virginia Power Co has not set a restart date for its 911 megawatt North Anna nuclear power unit 1 after an electrical problem automatically tripped the unit, a company spokesman said Thursday.
"It could be a matter of days (before startup), we just don't know at this point," said company spokesman Jim Norvelle.
Norvelle said the company was investigating the cause of the shutdown, which occured when an electrical relay to a generator opened, tripping the generator and then the reactor.
Investigations include the possibility of an electrical anomally outside the plant, perhaps from a power distribution system, the spokesman said.
While the Mineral, Va., unit is shut, workers will also examine a high-pressure turbine balance pipe for any signs of corrosion, he said.
The neighboring 909 megawatt North Anna unit 2 was shut Monday to replace a section of a high-pressure turbine balance pipe after two leaks were discovered, Norvelle said.
North Anna 2 was expected to return to service late Thursday, he said.

Virginia Power, a subsidiary of Dominion Resources, is the operator and has an 88.4 percent interest in the North Anna plant, while Old Dominion Electric Co-operative holds the remaining 11.6 percent.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
